Model parallelism and data parallelism are two different approaches used in distributed training to parallelize the training process. 

In data parallelism, the model is split across multiple devices, and each device processes a different subset of the data. This approach is often used when the model is too large to fit into the memory of a single device. In this case, the model parameters are split across the devices, and each device trains a different subset of the data. Knowledge distillation is a technique used in machine learning to create a smaller, faster model that can mimic the performance of a larger, more complex model. The idea is to train a smaller, simpler model (the student) to learn from the output of a larger, more complex model (the teacher) rather than from the raw input data. This allows the student model to be trained more quickly and with less computational resources, while still achieving similar performance to the teacher model on a given task.
